annals.title: The Crusaders take their vows
annals.summary: Sworn guards of Stendarr's temple, before the order ever left its doors. Thirty years later their First Keeper would write them a rule for a world beyond it.
annals.source: The Vigilant Rule of 4E 35, which opens by counting thirty years back to the vows.

annals.title: The Vigilant Rule is written
annals.summary: First Keeper Maurice of Glenpoint pens a codex for the newly founded Knights Vigilant, on the argument that Stendarr's Mercy does not stop at a temple door.
annals.source: The Rule itself, published on this site.

annals.title: The Blood-Score begins
annals.summary: Shield brother turned on shield sister over who should take the mantle of Harbinger, and it was decided that to claim Jorrvaskr was to prove the claim. Twenty years of infighting followed.
annals.source: The Companions' own account, which dates it relative to today rather than by year.

annals.title: The White-Gold Concordat
annals.summary: The Great War ends on terms that hold on paper and in very little else. Everything Mereth plays is downstream of this document.
annals.source: The setting itself: Mereth plays 4E 185, ten years after the Concordat.

annals.title: Plague takes the proud families of the Pale
annals.summary: It left the hold with precious few worthy challengers, and Varinn became the natural successor to his grand uncle.

annals.title: Kellanved Ultor takes Falkreath
annals.summary: Of House Ultor, raised to the seat after the sudden death of his father, Jarl Harvok.

annals.title: High King Varic Law-Giver dies at sea
annals.summary: His sword was found in the hands of Redguard pirates off High Rock. Skyrim has had no High King since, which is the fact behind most of the province's politics.

annals.title: Kellanved Ultor steps down
annals.summary: He left the seat of Falkreath with a published proclamation rather than quietly, and the court kept his record where it stood.

annals.title: Rigmyr Old-Pelt is raised in Falkreath
annals.summary: Chosen after Kellanved stepped down, which is how a seat changes hands here: in character, at a moot, and not by application.
